question: T12 (task-0088de1dbcce6ee8, task-ae80ef109abd8c4b): arrow keys on Wave Intensity under a second apart that end on the value they started from, and an arrow key right after Cmd+Z and Cmd+Shift+Z: is each an undo step, and what Cmd+Z then gives. On Blocks Probe at a 1600 by 1000 window, one new section per plan with a new Scrolling block and a Text block added after it, made on the desktop (desktop 1/2/3/26 and 1/2/3/10). The Scrolling block selected, Edit, Design ('open'), then keys through one DevTools session (rawKeyDown and keyUp; Cmd+Z and Cmd+Shift+Z as the key z with Meta, and Meta and Shift), the state read 60 ms after each key, at its gap and 1.2 s after the last ('after'); then Escape ('go') and Cmd+Z ('Z', only while the section is not back as built), a read after each. J: from the value as added (0), a press on the range's thumb at the value it shows, ArrowRight then ArrowLeft 300 ms apart. L: a press on Wave Intensity at 90, then J's keys. M: 90, a thumb press and one ArrowRight (1.2 s), then with no press Cmd+Z, Cmd+Shift+Z and ArrowRight 300 ms apart, the range keeping the focus. N: 90, a thumb press, then ArrowRight, Cmd+Z, Cmd+Shift+Z and ArrowRight 200 ms apart, all within a second of the first key. R5 ran J, L, M; R6 M, L, J; R7 and R8 N. Nothing saved: every session left by Exit Without Saving.
readsAre: reads: as CAP-T12WAVEKEYS (layout of the Scrolling block and every block in its section, the section rows in the view shown, the line, Undo and Redo; 'wave' the panel's Wave Intensity value while it is open). keys: for each run of keys, the value it started from (v0), the keys ([key, modifiers 4 Meta 8 Shift, gap ms]) and the states (the range's value, the focus, Undo and Redo, the selected blocks and the lines), named by the key and its place.
answer: L, desktop: 90 (1/2/5/26, the section 10 rows), then ArrowRight (120) and ArrowLeft (back to 90) 300 ms apart: the range keeps the focus, Undo on and Redo off after each key and 1.2 s after. Escape keeps it. The first Cmd+Z changes nothing that shows (1/2/5/26, 10 rows, the block 153.4 high) and turns Redo on; the second takes 90 back (1/2/3/26, 8 rows). So the two keys leave one undo step that ends where it began.

J, desktop: from 0 as added, ArrowRight (30) and ArrowLeft (0) 300 ms apart leave the areas and rows as built. In R6, which started with Redo on from L's Cmd+Z, the first key turned Redo off. No Cmd+Z was read for J: the section was back as built.

M, desktop: 90, ArrowRight (120; the block 154 high, the areas as at 90), then Cmd+Z with the focus on the range takes the key back (90, Undo and Redo on), Cmd+Shift+Z brings it back (120, Redo off) and ArrowRight 300 ms later takes 150 (1/2/6/26, the Text block 4/2/6/10, 11 rows). The range keeps the focus through all three. After Escape the first Cmd+Z gives 120 (1/2/5/26, the block 154 high, the Text block back on 3/2/5/10), the second 90 (153.4), the third the section as built. So a key right after Cmd+Shift+Z is a step of its own: it does not join the step that came back.

N, desktop: 90, then ArrowRight (120), Cmd+Z (90, Redo on), Cmd+Shift+Z (120, Redo off) and ArrowRight (150; 1/2/6/26, the Text block 4/2/6/10, 11 rows) 200 ms apart, the range keeping the focus. After Escape the first Cmd+Z gives 120 (1/2/5/26, the block 154 high), the second 90 (153.4), the third the section as built. So even under a second after the last key, a key after Cmd+Shift+Z is a step of its own: Cmd+Z and Cmd+Shift+Z end the run of keys that joins one step.
R5 and R6 read alike in every read and key state of J, L and M, apart from Redo at a plan's start (left on by the plan before); R7 and R8 alike in every read and key state of N.
